thunder noun and verb

classical

Traupman 136, 394

1tonitrus: second vowel unmarked (Lewis & Short marks it doubtful). The fourth-declension genitive -ūs is certain.

tonitrus1, tonitrūs m.

noun, fourth declension

Other words

  • tonat, tonāre, tonuit — it thunders

    classical · Traupman 137, 394

Examples

  • Nōlī timēre: tonitrus sonat tantum, nōn nocet.

    Don’t be afraid: thunder only makes a noise, it doesn’t hurt.composed

See also lightning, thunderbolt, storm.

SourcesLewis & Short: tono · Lewis & Short: tonitrus

John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, supplied PDF (printed page numbers): pp. 136–137, 394.
